title: Noun sentence - Order of the components
description: The natural order of the 3 components of a noun sentence (جُمْلَة اسْمِيَّة), Mubtada + Khabar + Muta'allaq bil khabar, and the two allowed abnormal orders (مُقَدَّم and مُؤَخَّر) that add exclusivity. Every example is a Quranic ayah with its reference.
source: Owner's lesson notes: Noun sentence, three lessons (finding the invisible "is", the 3 components, abnormal order)

questions.text: In إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ (Al-Infitar 82:13), what is the Mubtada?
questions.explanation: When a harf of Nasb is present, the Mubtada is the harf of Nasb and its ism together, so it is إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ: "Surely the righteous are in bliss".

questions.text: In وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ (Al-Baqarah 2:19), which part is the Muta'allaq bil khabar?
questions.explanation: اللَّهُ is the Mubtada and مُحِيطٌ is the Khabar. بِالْكَافِرِينَ is a Jaar Majroor that adds information, so it is the Muta'allaq bil khabar: "Allah is surrounding the disbelievers".

questions.text: In إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ (Al-Hijr 15:45), which component is not written in the ayah?
questions.explanation: إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ is the Mubtada and فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ is a Jaar Majroor, the Muta'allaq bil khabar. The Khabar is implied ("present"): "Surely the righteous are (present) in gardens and springs".

questions.text: What is the natural order of the 3 components of a noun sentence?
questions.explanation: The Mubtada comes first, then the Khabar, then the Muta'allaq bil khabar: M + K + MBK. A change in this order adds extra meaning to the sentence.

questions.text: What do we call a component that comes before its normal position?
questions.explanation: A component that comes earlier than its place in the natural order M + K + MBK is مُقَدَّم (muqaddam).

questions.text: What do we call a component that comes after its normal position?
questions.explanation: A component that comes later than its place in the natural order M + K + MBK is مُؤَخَّر (muakkhar).

questions.text: Which two abnormal orders are allowed in a noun sentence?

options.text: MBK (muqaddam) + M (muakkhar), and M + MBK (muqaddam) + K (muakkhar)
K (muqaddam) + M (muakkhar), and MBK + K + M
MBK (muqaddam) + K (muakkhar), and K + M + MBK
M + K + MBK, and K + MBK + M

questions.explanation: Only two abnormal orders are allowed: the Muta'allaq bil khabar moves before the Mubtada (MBK + M), or it moves before the Khabar (M + MBK + K). In both, the MBK is the muqaddam.

questions.text: The order of a noun sentence changes for 4 reasons. For the reason we study here, exclusivity, where does the word ONLY go in the translation?

options.text: After the last word of the sentence
Before the component that is muqaddam
Before the component that is muakkhar

questions.explanation: To show exclusivity, put ONLY before the muqaddam component, as in لِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ: "Praise is ONLY for Allah".

questions.text: What is the order of the components in وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ (Al-Baqarah 2:95)?

options.text: M + K + MBK, the natural order

questions.explanation: اللَّهُ (M), then عَلِيمٌ (K), then بِالظَّالِمِينَ (MBK). Nothing has moved, so this is the natural order: "Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers".

questions.text: What is the order of the components in وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:282)?

options.text: M + K + MBK, the natural order

questions.explanation: اللَّهُ is the Mubtada. The Muta'allaq bil khabar بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ comes before its normal place (muqaddam), and the Khabar عَلِيمٌ comes after its normal place (muakkhar).

questions.text: In إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:20), which component is muakkhar?

options.text: عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ, the Muta'allaq bil khabar
None; it is in the natural order

questions.explanation: The order is M (إِنَّ اللَّهَ) + MBK (عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ) + K (قَدِيرٌ). The MBK has moved before the Khabar, so the MBK is muqaddam and the Khabar قَدِيرٌ is muakkhar.

questions.text: Compare وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ (Al Imran 3:153) with وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (Al Imran 3:180). Which statement is right?

options.text: Both are in the natural order
3:153 has the Muta'allaq bil khabar muqaddam; 3:180 is natural
3:153 is natural; in 3:180 بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ is muqaddam and خَبِيرٌ is muakkhar

questions.explanation: In 3:153 the order is M + K + MBK. In 3:180 the Jaar Majroor بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ moves before the Khabar خَبِيرٌ, giving the allowed order M + MBK (muqaddam) + K (muakkhar).

questions.text: What is the order of the components in إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ (Al-Asr 103:2)?

options.text: M + MBK with the Khabar implied, the natural order

questions.explanation: إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ (M) comes first and لَفِي خُسْرٍ (MBK) after it, with the Khabar implied ("present"). The Mubtada is still first, so nothing is muqaddam: "Surely man is (present) in loss".

questions.text: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ (Al-Fatihah 1:2) is in the natural order. Which translation fits فَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ (Al-Jathiyah 45:36)?

options.text: So Allah ONLY is the praise.
So all praise is for Allah.
So ONLY praise is for Allah.
So praise is ONLY for Allah.

questions.explanation: لِلَّهِ, the Muta'allaq bil khabar, has moved before the Mubtada الْحَمْدُ (MBK muqaddam + M muakkhar). For exclusivity, ONLY goes before the muqaddam part: "praise is ONLY for Allah".

questions.text: What is the order of the components in وَعِنْدَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ (Al-Anam 6:59)?

options.text: M + K + MBK, the natural order

questions.explanation: عِنْدَهُ is a special mudhaaf with its mudhaaf ilaih, so it is the Muta'allaq bil khabar, and it comes before the Mubtada مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ: "With Him ONLY are the keys of the unseen".

questions.text: In وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ (Al Imran 3:28), which component is muakkhar?

options.text: إِلَى اللَّهِ, the Muta'allaq bil khabar
None; it is in the natural order

questions.explanation: الْمَصِيرُ is the Mubtada, so its normal place is first; it comes after إِلَى اللَّهِ, so it is muakkhar and إِلَى اللَّهِ is muqaddam: "The return is ONLY to Allah".

questions.text: Which translation shows the exclusivity in لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ (Al-Kafirun 109:6)?

options.text: You have your religion, and I have mine.
For you ONLY is your religion, and for me ONLY is my religion.
ONLY your religion is for you, and ONLY my religion is for me.
Your religion is for you, and my religion is ONLY for me.

questions.explanation: In both halves the Jaar Majroor (لَكُمْ, لِيَ) comes before the Mubtada (دِينُكُمْ, دِينِ): MBK muqaddam + M muakkhar. ONLY goes before the muqaddam part each time.

questions.text: Which of these is in the natural order M + K + MBK?

options.text: لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ (Al-Baqarah 2:284)
إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (Al Imran 3:119)

questions.explanation: In 3:119, إِنَّ اللَّهَ (M), عَلِيمٌ (K) and بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (MBK) are in their normal places. In 2:284 and 2:115 the MBK لِلَّهِ is before the Mubtada, and in 2:282 بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ is before the Khabar.

questions.text: In إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:143), which component is muqaddam?
questions.explanation: The Jaar Majroor بِالنَّاسِ comes before the Khabar لَرَءُوفٌ, so the order is M + MBK (muqaddam) + K (muakkhar). The Mubtada إِنَّ اللَّهَ is first, which is its normal place.

questions.text: Which translation fits وَلِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ (Al-Baqarah 2:115)?

options.text: And the east and the west are for Allah and others.
And ONLY the east and the west belong to Allah.
And to Allah ONLY belong the east and the west.
And the east belongs to Allah, ONLY the west.

questions.explanation: لِلَّهِ, the Muta'allaq bil khabar, comes before the Mubtada الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ, so it is muqaddam. For exclusivity, ONLY goes with the muqaddam part: "to Allah ONLY".
